music_content_accompany_332_about: The right hand runs down the chord in groups of three, three and two. The root lands with each group.
music_content_accompany_alberti_about: Low, high, middle, high in the left hand, the right hand's chord on 1 and 3.
music_content_accompany_ballad_about: The left hand climbs root, fifth, octave and tenth twice a bar under a held right-hand chord.
music_content_accompany_block_13_about: The root and the chord together on beats 1 and 3.
music_content_accompany_block_1_about: Both hands strike the chord on beat 1 and hold the bar: the root below, the chord above.
music_content_accompany_boogie_about: Eight to the bar, up the chord and back (1 3 5 6 b7 6 5 3) and swung, with right-hand chords on 2 and 4.
music_content_accompany_broken_about: The right hand rocks up and down the chord in eighths over a held root.
music_content_accompany_chart_1_about: Eight bars of triads, one a bar, closing on V and I.
music_content_accompany_chart_2_about: Sevenths join the triads, and some bars change chord on beat 3.
music_content_accompany_chart_2_label: Chart 2: two chords in some bars
music_content_accompany_chart_3_about: Sus and add9 colours and slash chords (the bass named after the slash).
music_content_accompany_chart_3_label: Chart 3: sus, add9 and slash bass
music_content_accompany_comp_and24_about: Red Garland's offbeats: the and of 2, then the next chord early on the and of 4.
music_content_accompany_comp_and2_4_abou: Short stabs on the and of 2 and on 4, room for a line on top.
music_content_accompany_comp_bossa_about: On 1, the and of 2 and 4, straight eighths.
music_content_accompany_comp_hardbop_abo: Short hits with the drummer: on 1, the and of 2, then the next chord pushed on the and of 4.
music_content_accompany_comp_waltz1_abou: Jazz waltz comping in 3/4: on 1, then the and of 2.
music_content_accompany_comp_waltz2_abou: In 3/4, leave 1 to the bass and comp on 2 and 3.
music_content_accompany_comp_whole_about: One chord a bar, on 1, held.
music_content_accompany_gospel_about: The chord, its IV over the same bass on the and of 2, and back on 4: the gospel and rock 1-4-1.
music_content_accompany_half_time_about: Root and chord on 1, then the next bar's chord pushed early on the and of 4.
music_content_accompany_lead_1_about: Quarters and eighths, chord tones on 1 and 3, played swung.
music_content_accompany_lead_2_about: Eighth-note lines and anticipations: the and of 4 tied into the next chord.
music_content_accompany_left_rootless_ab: Rootless A or B (3 5 7 9 or 7 9 3 5) on each chord and each bar line, whichever moves least.
music_content_accompany_left_roots_about: The root on each chord and each bar line.
music_content_accompany_left_shells_abou: Root and 7th (root and 5th on a triad) on each chord and each bar line.
music_content_accompany_lh_137_about: Left hand: root, 3rd, 7th (the 5th on a triad).
music_content_accompany_lh_173_about: Left hand: root, 7th, then the 3rd on top.
music_content_accompany_lh_alt_about: Left hand: 1-3-7 or 1-7-3, whichever moves least from the chord before.
music_content_accompany_lh_octave_about: Left hand: the root in octaves, short, with the right hand (Horace Silver's punches). Right hand: rootless A or B.
music_content_accompany_lh_root_then_abo: Left hand: the root. Right hand: rootless A or B.
music_content_accompany_lh_rootless_abou: Left hand: 3 5 7 9 or 7 9 3 5 (3 13 7 9 or 7 9 3 13 on a dominant), whichever moves least. The bass player has the root.
music_content_accompany_lh_two_feel_abou: Left hand: root on 1, fifth on 3. Right hand: the 3rd and 7th on the rhythm.
music_content_accompany_pop_sync_about: Both hands together on 1, the and of 2, and 4.
music_content_accompany_r58_about: The left hand walks root, fifth, octave, fifth in quarters under a held right-hand chord.
music_content_accompany_rock_about: Left-hand octaves on every eighth, the right hand's chord on 1 and 3.
music_content_accompany_shuffle_about: The rock and roll left hand: root and fifth, root and sixth, in swung eighths.
music_content_accompany_spread_about: The left hand opens root, fifth, tenth, fifth in quarters under a held right-hand chord.
music_content_accompany_stride_about: Left hand only: the root in octaves on 1, the chord on 2, a tenth on 3, the chord on 4.
music_content_accompany_stride_lite_abou: Left hand only: the root on 1, the chord on 2, the fifth on 3, the chord on 4.
music_content_accompany_under_melody_abo: The left hand on roots. On each chord change the right hand adds the chord below the melody note.
music_content_analysis_rule_backdoor: A backdoor: bVII7 going up a step to I. The iv7 before it pairs with it.
music_content_analysis_rule_dominant: The V: a dominant that resolves down a fifth to the key's I, or a ii-V left hanging. A hanging ii-V names the key a fifth below.
music_content_analysis_rule_ii: The ii of a ii-V: a minor (or half-diminished) chord a fourth below the V.
music_content_analysis_rule_other: Not part of a cadence. It's named in the last key reached, or in the next key when it's none of the last key's chords. iv and bVI count as borrowed from the minor.
music_content_analysis_rule_passing_dim: A passing diminished 7th: it links two chords a step apart.
music_content_analysis_rule_related_ii: A related ii: the ii before a secondary dominant or a tritone sub.
music_content_analysis_rule_secondary: A secondary dominant: it resolves down a fifth to a chord that isn't a key's I. It belongs to that chord's key.
music_content_analysis_rule_tonic: A key's I: the home chord, or a major chord reached from its own V7, tritone sub or backdoor. A minor i needs its whole iiø7 V7 and two bars.
music_content_analysis_rule_tritone_sub: A tritone sub: a dominant that resolves down a half step, in place of the V a tritone away.

music_content_catalog_chords_blurb: Fret an open chord string by string, strum it, or change between two chords in time.

music_content_catalog_ear_song_loops_blu: Hear a song's chord loop as a groove after the key is set and name every chord.
music_content_catalog_ear_wrong_note_blu: Follow a written melody by ear and find the note that was played wrong.
music_content_catalog_feel_blurb: Hear a groove and say whether it is straight, swung, a shuffle or in 12/8.
music_content_catalog_fretboard_blurb: Work finger patterns, box shapes, note names and intervals on the neck.
music_content_catalog_jam_blurb: Solo over a progression with the chord tones lit for each chord.
music_content_catalog_lab_blurb: Play freely and record everything, with or without a backing track.

music_content_catalog_listening_blurb: Hear a loop flat and changed, and name the change: an EQ band, a level, a pan, compression or a delay.

music_content_catalog_phrases_blurb: Popular short phrases for your instrument: famous public-domain tunes and a style's stock licks, heard and played back.

music_content_catalog_two_hand_blurb: Each hand plays its own part: a steady pulse under a moving line, or both hands mirroring.

music_content_jazz_chord_scale_dom7_alte: The most tension, over the V of a minor ii-V-i. Think of Db melodic minor.
music_content_jazz_chord_scale_dom7_bebo: Mixolydian plus a major 7th as a passing note.
music_content_jazz_chord_scale_dom7_half: Adds the b9, #9 and #11 over a V7.
music_content_jazz_chord_scale_dom7_whol: For dominant chords with a raised 5th (7#5).
music_content_jazz_chord_scale_m7b5_alte: A brighter half-diminished sound. Think of Eb melodic minor.
music_content_jazz_chord_scale_m7b5_locr: Think of the major scale a half step above: Db major over Cm7b5.
music_content_jazz_chord_scale_maj7_bebo: The major scale plus a raised 5th as a passing note.
music_content_jazz_chord_scale_maj7_lydi: Brighter than major: the 4th is raised (#11), so it never rubs against the chord's 3rd.
music_content_jazz_chord_type_dim7_role: A passing chord: stacked minor 3rds (C Eb Gb A).
music_content_jazz_chord_type_dom7_role: The V chord of a ii-V-I. Takes every altered extension (b9 #9 #11 b13).
music_content_jazz_chord_type_m7_role: The ii chord of a major ii-V-I.
music_content_jazz_chord_type_m7b5_role: The ii chord of a minor ii-V-i.
music_content_jazz_chord_type_maj6_role: A brighter tonic than maj7. The 6th replaces the 7th.
music_content_jazz_chord_type_maj7_role: The I chord of a major ii-V-I.
music_content_jazz_chord_type_min6_role: A tonic minor with a major 6th, not b6. A common minor i chord.
music_content_jazz_chord_type_mmaj7_role: The i chord of a minor ii-V-i. With a 9th, "the James Bond chord".
music_content_jazz_comping_blue_third_c7: Blue third over a C7 shell
music_content_jazz_comping_blue_third_f7: Blue third over a F7 shell
music_content_jazz_comping_blue_third_g7: Blue third over a G7 shell
music_content_jazz_dominant_voicing_alte: The most tension, so it resolves strongly.
music_content_jazz_extension_11_note: The 4th, an octave up. Use over m7 and V7.
music_content_jazz_extension_13_note: The 6th, an octave up. V7 only.
music_content_jazz_extension_sharp11_not: The lydian colour. Use over maj7 and V7.
music_content_jazz_lick_10_tip: Add 8th-note rests to vary the rhythm.
music_content_jazz_lick_11_tip: A sequence: a repeating melodic shape moving up or down.
music_content_jazz_lick_12_tip: The ii-V-I-VI loops: the A7 resolves back to Dm7. Loop it to practise improvising.
music_content_jazz_lick_13_tip: Start lines from any note. A chromatic enclosure leads into the A7.
music_content_jazz_lick_14_tip: Half-step approach into G7alt. Chord-tone solo (1 3 5 7 9) over A7b9.
music_content_jazz_lick_15_tip: Diminished over G7. A chromatic enclosure leads into the A7.
music_content_jazz_lick_17_tip: Half-step approaches Bb to B and Eb to E. A chromatic enclosure leads into the A7.
music_content_jazz_lick_18_tip: Chord-tone solo (1 3 5 7 9). Over a minor ii-V-i, the scale changes on each chord.
music_content_jazz_lick_1_tip: Solo using only the 1 3 5 7 of each chord.
music_content_jazz_lick_21_tip: Half-step-below approaches: C# to D and F# to G.
music_content_jazz_lick_25_tip: Minor-chord lick in straight time. Half-step-below approach (B to C, E to F).
music_content_jazz_lick_2_tip: The C major scale works over all three chords of a major ii-V-I.
music_content_jazz_lick_30_tip: Box 1 at the twelfth fret, three fingers. Land the D on beat 3 of bar 1 and let it ring.
music_content_jazz_lick_31_tip: The same shape, fingers and strings at the fifth fret. A transfer, not a new lick.
music_content_jazz_lick_3_tip: Add a triplet to vary the rhythm. The bebop chromatic note is Gb. End lines on 1 3 5 or 7 (C E G B).
music_content_jazz_lick_4_tip: Half-step-below approach into the changes: Bb to B and Eb to E.
music_content_jazz_lick_5_tip: The approach is most effective at the chord change. Aim for the chord's major 3rd.
music_content_jazz_lick_6_tip: The half-step-below approach works into all 7 scale notes (F# to G, D# to E).
music_content_jazz_lick_7_tip: Play inside (C major), then outside over the V7 (G diminished: b9 #9 #11), then back inside.
music_content_jazz_technique_bebop_scale: Add a chromatic passing note. Dominant bebop is mixolydian plus a major 7th. Major bebop is major plus a #5. Minor bebop is dorian plus a major 7th or major 3rd.
music_content_jazz_technique_chord_tone_: Build lines from the 1 3 5 7 (and 9) of each chord. The safest, strongest note choices.
music_content_jazz_technique_chromatic_e: Surround a target note from above and below before landing on it.
music_content_jazz_technique_half_step_b: Play the note a half step below a chord tone, then the chord tone: Bb to B, Eb to E. Aim for the major 3rd, right at the chord change.
music_content_jazz_technique_lh_textures: Stride (bass note then chord), bossa-nova bass (root and 5th), paradiddle (L R L R) and 4-note cell patterns.
music_content_jazz_technique_parent_scal: The C major scale works over every chord of a C-major ii-V-I. Aim to land lines on 1 3 5 or 7.
music_content_jazz_technique_rhythmic_va: Add triplets and 8th-note rests so lines don't sound mechanical.
music_content_jazz_technique_sequence_su: Repeat a melodic shape, moving it up or down the scale.
music_content_jazz_technique_start_from_: Start lines on the 9th, 3rd or 4th, not always the root. It varies the contour.
music_content_jazz_technique_v7_scale_ch: Over the V7, switch to the diminished (half-whole) or altered scale. That adds b9 #9 #11 b13 tension. Then resolve back into the key.
music_content_jazz_vocab_lick_101_tip: Into the 3rd of Cmaj7: F above, D# below, then E on the downbeat.
music_content_jazz_vocab_lick_102_tip: Into the root: a half step above (Db) and a half step below (B), then C.
music_content_jazz_vocab_lick_103_tip: Into the 5th: A above, F# below, then G.
music_content_jazz_vocab_lick_104_tip: An enclosure into each change: C and A# around G7's 3rd, then F and D# around Cmaj7's 3rd.
music_content_jazz_vocab_lick_105_tip: The blue 3rd (Eb) slides into the major 3rd, then up the chord.
music_content_jazz_vocab_lick_106_tip: The bebop dominant scale down from C: the passing B keeps the chord tones on the beat, landing on F7's 3rd.
music_content_jazz_vocab_lick_107_tip: Up the blues scale through the b5, back down to the root.
music_content_jazz_vocab_lick_108_tip: Bar 5 back to bar 7: Ab is the blue note over F7, then C7's 3rd on the downbeat.
music_content_jazz_vocab_lick_109_tip: Bars 9 to 11: up and down each chord, the b9 (Ab) passing on G7.
music_content_jazz_vocab_lick_110_tip: A riff and its answer: the same start, a different ending.
music_content_jazz_vocab_lick_111_tip: A fast bluesy run down the blues scale, then the blue 3rd resolving up.
music_content_jazz_vocab_lick_112_tip: A phrase up high answered low down in the bass, the way Silver answers his own lines.
music_content_jazz_vocab_lick_113_tip: Crushed notes: the blue 3rd a sixteenth before the major 3rd, twice.
music_content_jazz_vocab_lick_114_tip: Giant Steps' first eight bars: 1-2-3-5 on every chord, the whole-bar chords up and back.
music_content_jazz_vocab_lick_115_tip: Giant Steps' last eight bars, the ii-Vs with a minor 3rd on the ii.
music_content_jazz_vocab_lick_116_tip: The Coltrane cycle in C: keys a major 3rd apart, each with its V7.
music_content_jazz_vocab_lick_117_tip: A I-vi-ii-V intro: four bars that set the key and hand the band the downbeat.
music_content_jazz_vocab_lick_118_tip: A iii-VI-ii-V tag: the last two bars played twice before the I.
music_content_jazz_vocab_lick_119_tip: A Basie-style ending: the cadence, then three soft plinks high up, the last on the root.
music_content_jazz_vocab_lick_120_tip: A bossa bass: the root on 1 and 3, the 5th just before each.
music_content_jazz_vocab_lick_121_tip: A two-beat gospel bass: the root and 5th on 1 and 3, walking between the chords.
music_content_jazz_vocab_lick_122_tip: A latin tumbao: the 5th on the and of 2, the next chord's root on 4.
music_content_jv_ask_spread: Play {symbol} as a spread, no root.
music_content_jv_close_about: A melody note on top with the next three chord tones close below it, through each chord tone of a ii-V-I. A major chord with the root on top takes the 6th.

music_content_jv_drop2_about: 4-way close with the second voice from the top dropped an octave into the left hand.
music_content_jv_drop2_name: {symbol} under a melody {mel}: drop the second voice from the top an octave, {notes}.
music_content_jv_evans_about: Bill Evans spreads on a ii-V-I: a three-note left hand (3-7-9, then 7-3-13 on the V) and two notes in the right, the melody with one voice under it.
music_content_jv_garland_about: A 12-bar blues: the left hand plays 3-7-9, the right hand the melody in octaves with the 5th inside.

music_content_jv_how_379_63: 3-7-9 in the left hand, the 6th and the 3rd in the right
music_content_jv_how_37_9513: 3-7 in the left hand, 9-5-13 in the right
music_content_jv_how_7313_95: 7-3-13 in the left hand, the 9th and the 5th in the right
music_content_jv_how_73_9513: 7-3 in the left hand, 9-5-13 in the right
music_content_jv_locked_about: George Shearing's block chords up the scale and back: the melody doubled an octave below in the left hand, 4-way close under it in the right, the I6 on chord tones and the diminished seventh on the passing notes.
music_content_jv_locked_name_passing: Melody {mel}: a passing note, so {chord} close under it ({notes}), and {mel} an octave down in the left hand.
music_content_jv_locked_name_tone: Melody {mel}: a chord tone, so {chord} close under it ({notes}), and {mel} an octave down in the left hand.
music_content_jv_monk_about: Thelonious Monk's shells on a 12-bar blues, the root in the left hand: 3-b7-1 on the I, and on the IV and V the 3rd and 7th with the root and b9 together on top, a half step apart.
music_content_jv_monk_name_i: {symbol}, bar {bar}: 3-b7-1, the root on top a whole step above the 7th ({notes}), the root in the left hand.
music_content_jv_monk_name_other: {symbol}, bar {bar}: 3-b7, then the root and b9 a half step apart on top ({notes}), the root in the left hand.
music_content_jv_quartal_about: Three-note stacks of 4ths in the left hand, moved up the dorian mode for two octaves, as McCoy Tyner comps.
music_content_jv_quartal_name: Stack of 4ths on {bottom}: {notes}, all in the left hand, every note in {group}.
music_content_jv_quartal_tune_about: Every chord in a tune's changes as a left-hand stack of two 4ths from the chord's scale, with its 3rd or 7th inside: 7-3-6 on a major 7th, 11-b7-b3 on a minor 7th, 5-1-4 on a 7sus.
music_content_jv_quartal_tune_ask: {symbol}: a left-hand stack of 4ths with its 3rd or 7th inside.
music_content_jv_sevenths_about: The seventh chord on each degree of the key, root position, up the key and back.
music_content_jv_sevenths_name: {symbol}, the {numeral}: root position, 1 3 5 7 from the bottom.
music_content_jv_slash_ask: {symbol} as a slash chord, the root lowest.
music_content_jv_slash_name_diminished: {symbol} as {slash}: {left} in the left hand, the {triad} diminished triad in the right ({adds}). Any inversion.
music_content_jv_slash_name_major: {symbol} as {slash}: {left} in the left hand, the {triad} major triad in the right ({adds}). Any inversion.
music_content_jv_slash_name_minor: {symbol} as {slash}: {left} in the left hand, the {triad} minor triad in the right ({adds}). Any inversion.
music_content_jv_slash_tune_about: Every chord in a tune's changes as a triad over its root, as Herbie Hancock voices them: the major triad a whole step below the root on a minor 7th (m11), a 7sus or a dominant (9sus), the triad on the 5th over a major 7th (maj9), the minor triad on the b3 over a half-diminished.
music_content_jv_so_what_about: Three 4ths and a major 3rd on top, moved through the dorian mode: two notes in the left hand, three in the right.
music_content_jv_so_what_ask: {group}: the So What chord with {bottom} at the bottom.
music_content_jv_so_what_name: So What chord on {bottom}: {notes}. 4ths up from {bottom} in {group}, a 3rd on top. {left} in the left hand.
music_content_jv_sus_about: Each 7sus as a slash chord: the root and 5th in the left hand, the major triad a whole step below the root in the right (C/D for D7sus). The Maiden Voyage set: up a minor 3rd, then down a whole step twice.
music_content_jv_sus_ask: Play {symbol} as a slash chord, the root lowest.
music_content_jv_sus_name: {symbol} as {slash}: {root} and {fifth} in the left hand, the {triad} triad in the right, any inversion.
music_content_jv_two_hand_about: ii-V-I with no root: the left hand plays 3-7 (7-3 on the V), the right hand 9, 5 and 13 above it.
music_content_jv_upper_about: Every dominant in a tune's changes: a 1-3-7 shell in the left hand and a triad on top. The II triad (9 #11 13) on a dominant going to major, the bVI (#9 b13) on one going to minor or marked altered, the VI (b9 13) on one marked b9.
music_content_jv_upper_ask: {symbol}: an upper-structure triad over a 1-3-7 shell.
music_content_jv_upper_name: {symbol}: the {numeral} triad, {triad} major, over a 1-3-7 shell. It adds {adds}. Any inversion on top.
music_content_loops_borrowed_hint: iv, bVI, bVII and bIII beside I, IV, V and vi.
music_content_loops_minor_hint: i, iv, v and V, with bVI, bIII and bVII from the natural minor.
music_content_loops_modal_hint: Dorian, Mixolydian, Lydian, Phrygian and Aeolian.
music_content_loops_pop_hint: I, IV, V and vi in the four loops pop is made of.
music_content_loops_rock_hint: bVII, bVI and bIII: the rock and Mixolydian loops.
music_content_loops_songs_hint: Real songs' chords, in a key you hear first.
music_content_loops_tritone_hint: bII7 to I against V7 to I.

music_content_piano_gospel_four_five_one: The bass walks 1-2-3-4 into IV, then V over the IV bass passes back to I/3.
music_content_piano_gospel_passing_dim_a: I-#Idim7-ii and IV-#IVdim7-I/5: a diminished chord a half step up joins two chords.
music_content_piano_gospel_slash_walk_ab: I, V/7, vi, vi/5, IV, I/3, ii7, V: the bass walks down while the right hand barely moves.
music_content_piano_lick_tip_19: The standard minor ii-V-i scale set: D locrian, G diminished or altered, C dorian.
music_content_piano_lick_tip_20: Locrian, diminished, then dorian: a new scale on each chord.
music_content_piano_lick_tip_26: Dorian over each chord: C dorian, then F dorian.
music_content_piano_lick_tip_28: Paradiddle texture, played here as one line.
music_content_reading_jazz_description: Jazz heads: chord tones on the beat, blue notes and chromatic approaches, anticipations of 1 and 3. Written straight, played swung.
music_content_reading_jazz_rhythm: swing eighths written straight, anticipations tied over the beat
music_content_reading_level_level_2_desc: Wider range, bass-clef option, and quicker movement.
music_content_reading_level_level_3_desc: Syncopation, dotted rhythms and leaps up to a fourth.
music_content_reading_line_4_description: One line at about ABRSM Grade 2 to 3: leaps to a fifth, scale and arpeggio fragments.
music_content_reading_line_4_rhythm: rests, ties, dotted quarter and eighth, 2/4 and 3/4
music_content_reading_line_5_description: One line at about ABRSM Grade 3 to 4: leaps to an octave, accidentals, pickups.
music_content_reading_line_6_description: One line at about ABRSM Grade 4 to 5: chromatic neighbour and passing notes, triplets.
music_content_reading_line_6_rhythm: syncopation over the beat and the sixteenth, dotted eighth and sixteenth, eighth triplets, 2/2 and 3/8
music_content_reading_piano_4_descriptio: Hands together at about ABRSM Grade 2: a five-finger melody over left-hand roots and fifths.
music_content_reading_piano_4_rhythm: dotted quarter and eighth, ties, quarter and half rests
music_content_reading_piano_5_descriptio: About ABRSM Grade 3: the right hand leaves the five-finger position, the left plays two-note chords.
music_content_reading_piano_6_descriptio: About ABRSM Grade 4: broken chords, Alberti and waltz bass, chromatic passing notes, pickups.
music_content_reading_piano_7_descriptio: About ABRSM Grade 5: chorale texture, a melody with a lower voice over left-hand chords.
music_content_reading_piano_7_rhythm: syncopation over the beat, dotted eighth and sixteenth
music_content_reading_piano_8_descriptio: About ABRSM Grade 6: right-hand octaves and three-note chords, triplets, the left hand moving into the treble clef, 9/8 and 5/4, longer phrases.
music_content_reading_piano_8_rhythm: eighth triplets, and all of the above in 9/8 and 5/4
music_content_reading_piano_9_descriptio: About ABRSM Grade 7: five sharps or flats, 7/8 and 5/8, triplets and sixteenth syncopation, wider leaps, clef changes. No 8va or tempo changes yet.
music_content_reading_piano_9_rhythm: 7/8 and 5/8 in their groups, quarter and eighth triplets, sixteenth syncopation

music_content_technique_song_boxer_note: Verse in C shapes with no capo. The recording sounds lower (a detuned guitar). The C to Am bass walk is dropped.
music_content_technique_song_dust_note: Verse progression. G/B is played as G. The intro's Cmaj7, Cadd9 and Asus2 colour chords are left out.
music_content_technique_song_everybody_h: Verse only (bass then strings 3 2 1 2 3). The walkdown and the Em A chorus are left out.
music_content_technique_song_hallelujah_: Capo 5 with G shapes (sounds in C). The first half of the verse. The roll is an approximation.
music_content_technique_song_house_note: The 8-bar verse is cut to 6 by merging the closing C E E into one E bar. No capo.
music_content_technique_song_landslide_n: Capo 3. G/B becomes G. The original is closer to an inside-out roll than true Travis.
music_content_technique_song_nothing_els: Only the verse chord loop. The intro's open-string melody and hammer-ons aren't included.
music_content_technique_song_scarborough: 3/4 in Am shapes (capo 7 to match the recording). G/B becomes G and the melody isn't included.
music_content_technique_song_tears_note: Slash bass notes (E/G#, A/E, D/F#) and E7sus4 are dropped. The song changes chord every two beats, and p i m a only approximates Clapton's picking.
music_content_technique_song_uke_cant_he: In C (the original is in D). 12/8 at a dotted quarter of about 66 BPM.
music_content_technique_song_uke_hallelu: 12/8 felt as 6/8. The taught version pinches strings 4 and 1 on each downbeat, so the roll is an approximation.
music_content_technique_song_uke_house_n: Thumb on string 4, then i m a. The verse is shortened to 6 bars.
music_content_technique_song_uke_scarbor: 3/4 in Am at a slower practice tempo with open strings ringing. The melody isn't included.
music_content_tunes_jazz_blues_composer: Traditional form (Bags' Groove, Now's the Time)
music_content_tunes_reharm_backdoor_abou: Reach the next chord from iv7 to bVII7 (Fm7 Bb7 to C).
music_content_tunes_reharm_chromatic_abo: Its second half becomes the ii-V a half step above the next chord (Ebm7 Ab7 to Dm7).
music_content_tunes_reharm_passing_dim_a: Its second half becomes a diminished 7th a half step below the next chord.
music_content_tunes_reharm_related_ii_ab: A dominant shares its time with its ii (G7 becomes Dm7 G7).
music_content_tunes_reharm_secondary_abo: The chord becomes the dominant of the chord after it (Am7 before Dm7 becomes A7).
music_content_tunes_reharm_tritone_about: A dominant becomes the dominant a tritone away (G7 to Db7).
music_content_tunes_rhythm_changes_compo: After George Gershwin's I Got Rhythm (Oleo, Anthropology)
